title: INPUT_PULLUP
summary: Wiring an external 10k resistor on your breadboard for every single button takes up space and requires extra jumper wires.

steps.title: INPUT_PULLUP

quickCheck.question: What is the primary benefit of configuring a pin with pinMode(pin, INPUT_PULLUP)?
options: It activates the Arduino's built-in pull-up resistor, eliminating the need for an external breadboard resistor
It turns the pin into a high-voltage motor output
It makes the Arduino run without USB power
quickCheck.explanation: `INPUT_PULLUP` uses the chip's internal 20k-50k resistor to hold the pin at 5V, reducing parts and wiring complexity.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: The microcontroller has internal pull-up resistors in silicon that can be enabled with `INPUT_PULLUP`.

quickCheck.question: When using INPUT_PULLUP, what does digitalRead(pin) return when nobody is touching the button?
options: HIGH (held at +5V by the internal pull-up)
quickCheck.explanation: When unpressed, the internal pull-up holds the pin securely at 5V (HIGH) with zero floating noise.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: The internal pull-up resistor pulls the pin voltage up to HIGH (+5V) when the switch is open.

options: It eliminates the need for external breadboard resistors

questions.question: With INPUT_PULLUP, what does digitalRead() return when the button IS pressed to GND?
questions.explanation: Active-low logic: pressing the button connects the pin to Ground, reading LOW!
